segments.he: הַהוֹלְכִין לַתַּרְפּוּת — אֲסוּרִין לָשֵׂאת וְלָתֵת עִמָּהֶם. אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: גּוֹי הַהוֹלֵךְ לַתַּרְפּוּת, בַּהֲלִיכָה — אָסוּר, דְּאָזֵיל וּמוֹדֵי קַמֵּי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, בַּחֲזָרָה — מוּתָּר, מַאי דַהֲוָה הֲוָה.
segments.en: § The mishna teaches: With regard to «those going to a festival of idolatry,» it is «prohibited to engage with them in business.» The Gemara notes that «Shmuel says:» In the case of «a gentile who goes to a festival of idolatry,» if he is «on» his «way to» the festival «it is prohibited» to engage in business with him, «as he» subsequently «goes and» offers «thanks before» the object of «idol worship. Upon» his «return it is permitted,» as «what was, was,» i.e., he has already finished his worship, and refraining from engaging in business with the gentile at this stage will accomplish nothing.
